full_reasoning:
<think>**chain of thought**
</think>
Antibiotic resistance arises through natural selection, a cornerstone of evolutionary biology. When antibiotics are used, they kill most bacteria, but some may possess genetic mutations that allow them to survive. These resistant bacteria then reproduce, passing on their resistance traits to subsequent generations. Over time, this leads to the proliferation of antibiotic-resistant strains. Overprescription of antibiotics accelerates this process by exposing more bacteria to these drugs, increasing the likelihood that resistant strains will emerge and spread. This misuse reduces the effectiveness of antibiotics, making infections harder to treat and posing a significant threat to public health.
